teaser: Two releases passed every check and never reached the site because the checks stopped at the git remote; a release now ends by asking the live site its version.
core_idea: Shipped is a fact about the reader, not about your repository, so a release has to verify the boundary the reader is on and not only the ones the repository can see.

nodes.label: Two releases that never reached anybody
nodes.summary: Two consecutive releases pushed cleanly, printed both remotes in sync, and the site served a two-release-old page for forty minutes until a human on a phone asked if it was the latest version.

nodes.label: The version badge
nodes.summary: The badge on the home page that a human looked at to notice the miss, and that the release now polls for the new version.

nodes.label: Checking the wrong boundary
nodes.summary: The checks were not weak; they were checking the wrong boundary.

nodes.label: What the release actually verified
nodes.summary: Build the site, run the validator, commit and push the encrypted vault and confirm sync, commit and push the git mirror and confirm HEAD equals origin/dev.

nodes.label: The bytes arrived at GitHub
nodes.summary: HEAD == origin/dev compares hashes, not hopes, but it means the bytes arrived at GitHub, not that anybody can read them.

nodes.label: Three boundaries, two verified
nodes.summary: Source to git remote, git remote to Pages deploy, Pages deploy to the reader; a GitHub Actions job sits in the unverified gap and reports into a system neither remote knows about.

nodes.label: What actually failed
nodes.summary: The deploy job died in Set up job because codeload.github.com rate-limited the download of actions/configure-pages with a 429, while the validate and tag-release jobs passed.

nodes.label: The most likely thing to break is not your code
nodes.summary: It is a piece of shared infrastructure you do not run, on a day you were not thinking about it.

nodes.label: Ask the live site what version it is serving
nodes.summary: A release now polls sgit.ai with a cache-buster for the new version, up to eight minutes, and aborts loudly if it never appears, naming the Actions page.

nodes.label: Shipped is a fact about the reader
nodes.summary: Shipped is a fact about the reader, not about your repository.

nodes.label: Three rules of the same shape
nodes.summary: A page nothing links to, a page the machine index omits, and a page the deploy never served are all unpublished, and the build or the release fails on each.

nodes.label: What this does not fix
nodes.summary: It detects a failed deploy but does not repair one, it checks only the home page's badge so a partial deploy would pass, and it adds up to eight minutes to every release.

quotes.text: The checks were not weak. They were checking the wrong boundary.
quotes.why: The diagnosis: strong checks on the wrong side of the deploy.

quotes.text: All three are the same claim: shipped is a fact about the reader, not about your repository.
quotes.why: The general rule the fix joins, learned from three failures of the same shape.
